chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Yahya ibn Masour, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Suweeq (barley flour porridge) and the broth of beef meat remove the vitiligo (white patches on the skin).

key_terms.السَّوِيقُ: Suweeq: A traditional dish made from barley flour, often cooked with water or milk.
key_terms.الْوَضَحِ: Al-Wadakh: Vitiligo or leukoderma, a condition causing white patches on the skin.
key_terms.مَرَقُ لَحْمِ الْبَقَرِ: Marqu Lahm al-Baqar: Broth or soup made from beef meat.

ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of eating Suweeq and beef broth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report from Imam al-Kazim (AS) highlights the practical medical wisdom of the Ahl al-Bayt, linking specific dietary interventions to the treatment of al-wadakh (vitiligo), a condition often associated with skin depigmentation. It reflects the broader Shia tradition of integrating prophetic medicine (al-Tibb al-Nabawi) with empirical observation, emphasizing that natural foods possess therapeutic properties ordained by God. The mention of beef broth alongside barley underscores the holistic approach to health in early Islamic society, where diet was viewed as a primary means of restoring bodily balance.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin ZIyad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Yahya Bin Masour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘
Al-Suweyq and the broth of the meat of the cow (beef soup), both do away with (remove)  the vitiligo’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘ from Yahya ibn Musawir who has said the following: “Abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
sawiq and broth of cow meat remove al-Bars (Albinism) illness.’”
